title: Thus Far the Lord Has Led Me on
description: Thus Far the Lord Has Led Me on in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 80, headed “An evening hymn, Psalm 4. 8. and 3. 5 6. and 143. 8”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thus far the Lord has led me on, Thus far his power pro-longs my days, And ev-ery eve-ning shall make known Some fresh memor-i-al of his grace.

lines: Thus far the Lord has led me on,
Thus far his power prolongs my days,
And every evening shall make known
Some fresh memorial of his grace.
Much of my time has run to waste,
And I perhaps am near my home;
But he forgives my follies past,
He gives me strength for days to come.
I lay my body down to sleep,
Peace is the pillow for my head,
While well-appointed angels keep
Their watchful stations round my bed.
In vain the sons of earth or hell
Tell me a thousand frightful things,
My God in safety makes me dwell
Beneath the shadow of his wings.
Faith in his name forbids my fear:
O may thy presence ne'er depart!
And in the morning make me hear
The love and kindness of thy heart.
Thus when the night of death shall come,
My flesh shall rest beneath the ground,
And wait thy voice to rouse my tomb,
With sweet salvation in the sound.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
